## C — Traffic signals, hybrid beacons and sign colors

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A39
An ordinary automated signal cycles through green, yellow, red and back to green. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A39
The handbook requires compliance with traffic signals except when an officer directs traffic or space is being made for emergency vehicles. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A39
Treat a dark intersection signal as an all-way stop when no peace officer, flagger or other traffic control is present. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A39
At a steady red signal, stop completely before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk and stay stopped while red, subject to the separately stated permitted-turn rules. [A39] [A40]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A39
A steady yellow warns that the signal is changing; if not yet in the intersection, make a safe stop. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A39
If already inside an intersection when yellow appears, continue through and clear it safely. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A39
Accelerating to get through before the signal changes is unlawful. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A39
Proceed on green only in the indicated direction and when the roadway is clear. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A39
A flashing red requires a full stop and yielding to approaching traffic and pedestrians before proceeding on a clear path. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A39
Stop for flashing red railroad-crossing lights even when no train can be seen. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A39
Proceed alertly and cautiously at a flashing yellow indication. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A39
A flashing yellow warning beacon calls attention to a sign or place requiring added attention or action. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A40
A red arrow requires a complete stop and prohibits a turn in the arrow's direction while it stays red. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A40
A steady yellow arrow warns of a change; if the intersection has not been entered, make a safe stop. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A40
If already in the intersection on a yellow arrow, continue in its direction and clear the intersection safely. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A40
Speeding up to get past a changing yellow arrow is unlawful. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A40
A flashing yellow arrow permits only its indicated movement, from the proper lane and with caution. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A40
Before moving on a flashing yellow arrow, yield to people in the adjacent crosswalk and other traffic in the intersection. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A40
Use a green arrow only from the appropriate lane, following its direction on a clear roadway. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A40
Before a permitted red-light turn, stop fully, look both ways and yield to pedestrians and other traffic. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A40
A right turn after stopping at a circular red is allowed unless a posted sign prohibits it. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A40
A left turn after stopping at a circular red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another, and may still be prohibited by signs. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A40
Red-arrow turns remain prohibited even where a circular-red turn could be allowed. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

Misconceptions: A circular red signal and a red arrow allow different turning decisions; an inactive midblock pedestrian beacon is different from an unstaffed dark intersection signal.
Mnemonics: Identify the indication, check the path, yield before proceeding.
Glossary: A hybrid beacon controls a marked pedestrian crossing; reversible-lane signals indicate whether a lane is open in the driver's direction.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.

## C2 — Traffic signals, hybrid beacons and sign colors

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A40
Reversible-lane signs and signals can change the direction a lane serves at different times of day. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A40
Do not use a lane displaying a red X. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A40
Leave a lane showing a steady yellow X as soon as it is safe because a red X will follow. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A40
A downward-pointing green arrow permits travel in that lane. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A41
A pedestrian hybrid beacon controls a marked crossing at an otherwise unsignalized location. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A41
The text describes a hybrid beacon as two red indications beside each other above a yellow indication. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A41
A hybrid pedestrian-beacon cycle begins with flashing yellow before changing to steady yellow. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A41
The steady-yellow stage of a hybrid beacon carries the meaning of an ordinary yellow signal. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A41
When both hybrid-beacon red lights are steady, drivers stop and remain stopped while pedestrians have WALK. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A41
After WALK ends, the hybrid beacon's red lights alternate while pedestrians receive flashing DON'T WALK. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A41
At alternating red hybrid-beacon lights, stop and confirm that neither your lane nor an adjacent lane contains a pedestrian before proceeding. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A41
A hybrid beacon goes dark after its pedestrian cycle finishes. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A41
The handbook exempts these dark midblock pedestrian beacons from the stop rule applying to a dark traffic signal. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A42
Red sign coloring is associated with stop, yield, do-not-enter and wrong-way messages. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A42
Yellow is the warning-sign color for unexpected roadway conditions. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A42
Yellow-green warnings identify pedestrian, bicycle, playground, school and school-bus contexts. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A42
Pink signs convey incident-management information. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A42
Green signs provide guidance such as directions and distances. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A42
Blue signs identify motorist services, including rest areas and hospitals. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A42
White signs communicate regulatory information such as speed restrictions. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A42
Orange signs warn about road workers and construction activity. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A42
Brown signs identify recreational and cultural destinations. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]
